Tesla's Cybercab Spotlights Halloween with Skeleton Passengers in Austin

Tesla's Halloween Cybercab Demonstration

Recent reports indicate that Tesla marked the Halloween season by deploying its steering-wheel-free Cybercab on public roads in Austin, Texas. According to circulating social media videos and company posts, the autonomous vehicle featured illuminated interior lighting and decorative skeleton passengers, drawing public attention.

Reported Features and Capabilities

Based on manufacturer specifications and reported demonstrations, the Cybercab is designed as a fully autonomous robotaxi without traditional driving controls.

  • No Manual Controls: The vehicle is built without a steering wheel, accelerator, or brake pedals, relying entirely on autonomous driving systems.
  • Cabin Design: Features upward-opening butterfly doors and a central touchscreen interface for controlling cabin climate, seating, and entertainment.
  • Storage and Sensors: Offers a reported rear boot space of 572 liters and utilizes exterior cameras to monitor surrounding traffic and roadways.

Availability and Public Reaction

The Cybercab operates as part of an expanding fleet in Texas. The Halloween stunt prompted various amused and intrigued reactions across social media platforms, with users commenting on the autonomous navigation and marketing approach.

Practical Implications and Verification

While viral videos showcase the vehicle navigating turns and traffic independently, independent safety verifications remain limited. Interested observers can verify original announcements and fleet updates through official Tesla channels and verified social media accounts.
